key_insight: ML-COHP predicts DFT-derived bond strengths from frozen MACE representations, reproducing grain-boundary ICOHP values to 0.06 eV in about a second.
engineering_relevance: Fast bond-strength estimates could accelerate analysis of grain boundaries, catalytic nanoparticles, and adsorbate-driven changes in metal bonding.
method: Extract frozen scalar and bond-projected vector descriptors from a MACE foundation model.
Use a symmetric pair head to correct an element-embedding-based bond baseline.
Combine with fine-tuned MACE geometries to examine bonding across O₂ coverages.
evidence_signal: Across high-entropy diborides, Pt/graphene, and O₂-covered Pt/Pd nanoparticles, errors for bonds stronger than 0.5 eV were 1.6–4.1%, about half those of a Gaussian-process comparator trained on the same data.
watch_item: Performance beyond the tested chemistries and structural environments remains unestablished; validate against DFT/LOBSTER before broader deployment.
paper_title: ML-COHP: predicting bond descriptors using latent space of a universal interatomic potentials
